questions.title: Binary search
questions.statement: Read a sorted array and a key. Print the key's index, or -1.
questions.input: n, n sorted integers, then the key.

examples.explain: Halve the range until the key or an empty range is found.

mistakes: Using <= mid instead of mid +/- 1, causing an infinite loop
hints: Compare the middle element and discard half.

questions.title: Bubble sort
questions.statement: Read n integers and print them sorted ascending using bubble sort.

examples.explain: Repeatedly swap adjacent out-of-order pairs.

mistakes: Looping j to n-1 instead of n-1-i, reading past the sorted tail
hints: After pass i, the last i elements are sorted.

questions.title: Selection sort
questions.statement: Read n integers and print them sorted ascending using selection sort.

examples.explain: Find the minimum of the unsorted suffix and swap it into place.

mistakes: Swapping inside the inner loop instead of after finding the minimum
hints: Track the index of the minimum, swap once per outer iteration.

questions.title: Insertion sort
questions.statement: Read n integers and print them sorted ascending using insertion sort.

examples.explain: Grow a sorted prefix by inserting each new value into place.

mistakes: Losing the key value while shifting
hints: Save a[i] before shifting larger values right.

questions.title: Remove duplicates
questions.statement: Read n integers and print the distinct values in first-seen order.

examples.explain: A LinkedHashSet keeps first-seen order and removes duplicates.

mistakes: Using a HashSet, which loses the first-seen order
hints: LinkedHashSet preserves insertion order.

questions.title: Second largest element
questions.statement: Print the second largest distinct value, or -1 if it does not exist.

examples.explain: Ignore values equal to the largest when updating the second.

mistakes: Updating second with a value equal to max
hints: Only update second when v is strictly below max.

questions.title: Rotate array right
questions.statement: Rotate the array right by k positions and print the result.
questions.input: n and k, then n integers.
questions.output: The rotated array separated by spaces.

examples.explain: Reduce k modulo n, then split at n-k.

mistakes: Not reducing k modulo n, causing an index out of range
hints: The new first element is at index n-k after reducing k.

questions.title: Merge two sorted arrays
questions.statement: Read two sorted arrays and print their merged sorted values.
questions.input: n m, then n integers, then m integers.

examples.explain: Walk both arrays with two pointers.

mistakes: Appending a trailing space that fails exact comparison
hints: Compare the two heads and append the smaller.

questions.title: Find the missing number
questions.statement: The numbers 1..n appear once except one missing value. Print the missing value.

examples.explain: Expected sum minus actual sum.

mistakes: Computing n*(n+1) in int and overflowing
hints: Use long for the expected sum.

questions.title: Find the duplicate number
questions.statement: Read n integers where exactly one value repeats. Print the repeated value.

examples.explain: A Set rejects the value it has already seen.

mistakes: Printing the first repeated position instead of the value
hints: add() returns false when the value is already present.

questions.title: Frequency of elements
questions.statement: Read n integers and print each distinct value and its count as value=count, sorted by value.

examples.explain: TreeMap keeps values sorted; merge counts them.

mistakes: Using HashMap and assuming the output order is stable
hints: TreeMap sorts keys for deterministic output.

questions.title: Two Sum
questions.statement: Find two numbers that add up to the target. Print their indices (i j with i < j), or -1.

examples.explain: Store seen values and look for target - current.

mistakes: Returning the same index twice when target is double the value
hints: Check for the complement before storing the current value.

questions.title: Anagram checker
questions.statement: Read two words and print Anagram if they contain the same letters with the same counts, else Not anagram.

examples.explain: Sort both words or compare 26 counts.

mistakes: Comparing arrays with == instead of Arrays.equals
hints: Sorting both makes equality a simple comparison.

questions.title: Character frequency
questions.statement: Read a word and print each character with its count as char=count, sorted alphabetically.

examples.explain: Use a 26-slot count array.

mistakes: Printing zero-count letters
hints: Only print slots with a positive count.

questions.title: First non-repeating character
questions.statement: Print the first character that appears exactly once, or none.

examples.explain: Count first, then scan in order for count 1.

mistakes: Using HashMap and losing the original character order
hints: LinkedHashMap preserves first-seen order.

questions.title: Reverse the words
questions.statement: Read a sentence and print its words in reverse order, separated by single spaces.

examples.explain: Split, then walk the array backwards.

mistakes: Keeping the original multiple spaces
hints: Trim and split on \\s+ first.

questions.title: Longest word
questions.statement: Print the longest word in a sentence; on a tie print the first one.

examples.explain: Compare lengths, keep the first on a tie.

mistakes: Using >= so the last tied word wins
hints: Strictly greater keeps the first on a tie.

questions.title: Matrix addition
questions.statement: Read two r×c matrices and print their element-wise sum.
questions.input: r c, then r*c integers for A, then r*c for B.
questions.output: r lines of c space-separated values.

examples.explain: Add matching positions.

mistakes: Printing a trailing space
hints: Read B in the same loop that prints the sum.

questions.title: Matrix multiplication
questions.statement: Read two n×n matrices and print their product.
questions.input: n, then n*n integers for A, then n*n for B.
questions.output: n lines of n space-separated values.

examples.explain: C[i][j] = sum of A[i][k] * B[k][j].

mistakes: Swapping the row/column indices in the inner sum
hints: Fix the output cell, then loop k over the shared dimension.

questions.title: Matrix transpose
questions.statement: Read an r×c matrix and print its transpose (c rows, r columns).

examples.explain: transpose[j][i] = matrix[i][j].

mistakes: Iterating rows in the outer loop, which prints the original
hints: The outer loop must walk columns.
